\section{Cohort}
Between March 2019 and October 2022 we enrolled 1,036 patients
with newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation at seven anticoagulation
clinics. An interim analysis was released to consortium members in 2024.
The median follow-up was 31 months. Baseline characteristics were
balanced across treatment strata after inverse-probability weighting.

\section{Regimens}
Patients received either a direct oral anticoagulant or dose-adjusted
warfarin according to clinician preference; crossover was documented
and analysed under an intention-to-treat convention.
Concomitant antiplatelet therapy was recorded at each visit.

\section{Outcomes}
The primary outcome was major bleeding as defined by the
international society criteria; secondary outcomes included
clinically relevant non-major bleeding and all-cause mortality.
Events were adjudicated by two blinded reviewers, with a third
reviewer resolving disagreements.

\section{Analysis}
Incidence rates were compared with cause-specific hazard models,
and sensitivity analyses repeated the comparisons in the
per-protocol cohort.
